To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the trigger conditions of soman‐ induced seizures were found to be related to the modulation of the gamma band energy, which is linked to the sympathetic response, in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the mechanisms involved in the triggering of seizures during soman intoxication in rats, and more precisely with the identification of the critical parameters leading to seizures, in order to understand the mechanisms of seizure induction and to develop new therapeutic approaches.
the study of the neurochemical and neurophysiological changes induced by soman in the central nervous system of the rat and with the analysis of their relationships.
the development of new therapeutic strategies against nerve agents, and more specifically against the organophosphate (OP) soman.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
soman‐induce seizures are triggered by a combination of AChE inhibition and ACh increase in the brain, which is not sufficient to predict seizures.
the epileptic fit is not directly related to the inhibition of cholinesterase or to the release of acetylcholine.
the threshold for the seizure‐inducing effect of soman in rats is a combination of the inhibition of brain cholinesterases and the increase of acetylcholine in the brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the seizure is triggered by a stress response, and not by the soman itself.
the trigger of soman‐ induced seizures is the stress response to intoxication, which may vary greatly between animals.
the seizure threshold is a complex phenomenon involving several parameters, and that a single parameter cannot predict the appearance of an epileptic fit after soman intoxication in rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gamma band energy is modulable by stress and that it might be related to a stress adaptation strategy.
the gamma band of the EEG, which is known to be associated with the arousal of the cortex, is a good marker of the risk for the occurrence of seizures during intoxication.
we can now use this technique in rats to determine the critical parameters which are necessary to predict seizure occurrence.
